hypothesis: If cave faunas are derived from their own continent's surface fauna, then troglobitic species in the Americas have their nearest surface relatives (same genus or, failing that, same family) in the Americas, and European troglobites have theirs in Europe, rather than American and European cave species being each other's closest relatives.
pass_criterion: Take a list of obligate-cave (troglobitic) species from the Americas and from Europe. For each species, use its genus and find the continents where surface (non-cave) congeners occur in GBIF georeferenced occurrences. The claim passes if at least 75% of cave species have a majority of their genus's surface-congener occurrence records on the cave species' own continent, or are in a genus endemic to that continent, and if fewer than 10% of genera contain cave species in both continents with the cave species lacking surface congeners on their own continent.
fail_criterion: The claim fails if fewer than 50% of cave species have surface relatives on their own continent, or if 25% or more of genera or families of cave species form cave-only lineages shared across America and Europe, with no surface relatives on the species' own continent.
interpretation: Darwin's "affinities" is read as taxonomic relationship at genus or family level. His "cave-animals of America" is read as obligate subterranean species, for example the Mammoth Cave fauna. "Europe" is read as the European continent. GBIF records locations, not phylogeny, so continental co-occurrence of congeners stands in for affinity. This is a modern reinterpretation. A phylogenetic follow-up would be stronger. Cave status would come from an external list of troglobites, such as the Subterranean Biodiversity literature. Fields used: scientificName, genusKey, familyKey, continent, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, countryCode, basisOfRecord.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence API (occurrence search)
dataset.why_it_fits: Open API over about 3.9 billion occurrence records. Each record has taxon keys at genus and family level and continent and country fields. These let us find where surface congeners of known cave species live. The www.gbif.org portal page returned 403, so the API endpoint was fetched instead. It returned a count of 3886670437. It has no DOI as a whole; derived downloads get their own DOIs.
